title: XOR.DDoS_Incident_Response_4fe
description: Investigate and contain the XOR.DDoS malware family and Groundhog backdoor on Linux servers.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity on its Linux servers. As an incident responder, your task is to investigate and contain the threat. The compromised systems may be part of a larger botnet involved in distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target server with the following credentials:
- Host: target (192.168.50.5)
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Activity
levels.content: Users have reported slow network performance. Investigate the target server for any suspicious network activity that could be causing this issue. Identify the port number (4444) used by the suspicious service.
levels.solution: Check running services and network connections. Identify the suspicious service listening on port 4444.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Consider checking the running services and network connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the 'ss' command to list all open ports and services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual or unexpected ports that are listening.

levels.title: Analyze Suspicious Service
levels.content: You've identified a suspicious service. Analyze it to determine its purpose and potential impact on the system. Identify the name of the suspicious service (bkd.service).
levels.solution: Examine the service configuration and related files. Identify the service named 'bkd.service' and its connection to the c2-server.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Consider examining the service configuration and related files.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the 'systemctl' command to check the status of the service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual or unexpected services that are running.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Check if the attacker has moved laterally to other systems within the network. Identify the name of the script (payload-transfer.sh) used for payload transfer.
levels.solution: Look for any unusual file transfers or remote connections. Discover the payload-transfer service and its connection to the next-target host.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Consider looking for any unusual file transfers or remote connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the 'ps' command to list all running processes.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual or unexpected processes that are running.
